=== NOTES 3:39 | Food Security – Nfsa 2013, Pds Reform, Buffer Stocks, One Nation One Ration Card, Pmgkay
## SUB 0 | National Food Security Act, 2013 – Coverage, Entitlements, Grievances
[39:0:0] # Enactment and nature
[39:0:1] - **Dates:** first an **Ordinance (5 July 2013)**; Act notified **10 Sep 2013** with effect from **5 July 2013** – the Act is of **2013** (not 2014, 2019, 2020).
[39:0:2] - **Nature:** welfare → **rights-based** approach; legal right to subsidised grain. Ministry: **Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution** (DFPD).
[39:0:3] - **Objective (long title):** **food and nutritional security** by ensuring access to adequate quality food at **affordable prices** so people can **live a life with dignity**. Distractors: "PDS Act", "FCI Act", "NFSA 2014".
[39:0:4] - **Coverage:** up to **75% of the rural** and **50% of the urban** population = about **two-thirds** of India; about **80-81 crore** people (not "50 crore"). Coverage is NOT limited to BPL families (Priority Households + AAY).
[39:0:5] - **Women:** the **eldest woman aged 18 or above** is head of household for the ration card (else the eldest male).
[39:0:6] # Entitlements
[39:0:7] TABLE head: Category | Entitlement | Issue price
  [39:0:7.0] Priority Household | 5 kg per person per month | ₹3 rice / ₹2 wheat / ₹1 coarse grain
  [39:0:7.1] Antyodaya Anna Yojana | 35 kg per household per month | Same; now free
  [39:0:7.2] Pregnant women and lactating mothers | Free meal during pregnancy and 6 months after + maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000 | –
  [39:0:7.3] Children 6 months-6 years | Take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi | –
  [39:0:7.4] Children 6-14 years | Mid-day meal / PM POSHAN | –
[39:0:8] - **Special focus on nutritional support to women and children** is a stated feature of the Act.
[39:0:9] - **Calorie trap (UPSC 2018):** the "take-home ration of 1,600 calories" for pregnant women is not in the Act (Schedule II norm is 600 kcal) – so only the eldest-woman statement is right.
[39:0:10] - **Issue prices** ₹3/2/1 **not revised since July 2013** while MSP and subsidy keep rising.
[39:0:11] - **Draft NFS (Amendment) Bill 2026** (DFPD, 24 June 2026): AAY → **7 kg per person, capped at 35 kg**; amends the first proviso to Sec 3(1); ends small households getting more grain per head.
[39:0:12] # Grievance and transparency
[39:0:13] TABLE head: Section | Mechanism
  [39:0:13.0] Sec 15 | Internal mechanism + District Grievance Redressal Officer (one per district); officials ignoring DGRO relief can be penalised
  [39:0:13.1] Sec 16 | State Food Commission in every State (Chairperson, five Members, Member-Secretary) – monitors and hears appeals; an existing commission may be designated
[39:0:14] - **Transparency:** **vigilance committees** at **State, district, block and Fair Price Shop** levels, **social audits**, mandatory disclosure of PDS records.
[39:0:15] > Statement angle: 75/50 coverage, eldest woman 18+, nutrition focus = correct; "only BPL", "50 crore covered", "1,600 calories" = wrong.
[39:0:16] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 10th ed. part 04 p.189-190 (NFSA highlights, 75/50, 5 kg at ₹3/2/1, AAY 35 kg, ₹6,000, eldest woman, DGRO, State Food Commission, vigilance committees); OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.28 (NFSA 2013 row); app notes 3:39 sub 3, 4, 6
## SUB 1 | Food Security – Concept, Dimensions and Entitlements
[39:1:0] # Definition
[39:1:1] - **World Food Summit 1996 / FAO:** food security exists when **all people, at all times**, have **physical and economic access** to **sufficient, safe and nutritious food** for an active and healthy life.
[39:1:2] - Food security does NOT mean access to "**the food of their choice**".
[39:1:3] # Dimensions
[39:1:4] TABLE head: Dimension | Meaning
  [39:1:4.0] Availability | Production + imports + previous years' stock in government granaries
  [39:1:4.1] Accessibility | Food within reach of every person
  [39:1:4.2] Affordability | Enough money to buy sufficient, safe, nutritious food
  [39:1:4.3] Absorption / utilisation | Body's ability to use the food
  [39:1:4.4] Stability | Access at all times
[39:1:5] - **NOT dimensions:** **Accountability**, price, **quantity of exports**.
[39:1:6] # National vs household
[39:1:7] TABLE head: Level | Meaning
  [39:1:7.0] National | Aggregate production + buffer stock (sufficient food stock)
  [39:1:7.1] Household | Each household can actually access and afford food
[39:1:8] - "**National but not household food security**" = **sufficient food stock, but not all households can get it** – hence PDS and NFSA.
[39:1:9] - Food security is needed **even in surplus years**: starvation comes from **unequal distribution and lack of access** (A-R: both true, R explains A).
[39:1:10] # Entitlement approach
[39:1:11] - **Amartya Sen**, *Poverty and Famines* (**1981**): famines come from a **collapse of entitlements** (command over food through income, exchange and transfers), not merely a fall in food availability; Sen added "**access**" to the 1970s "availability" idea.
[39:1:12] - **Per capita norms:** the APPSC 2011 key credits the **440 g/day foodgrain norm to FAO**; Indian nutrition bodies use about 400-420 g (ICMR/NIN) – treat 440 g as an exam figure only.
[39:1:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC 03 p.6-7 (availability, accessibility, affordability); OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.25 (World Food Summit, Sen's access); app notes 3:39 sub 0, 1
## SUB 2 | Public Distribution System – Aims, Evolution, AAY and Laws
[39:2:0] # Aims
[39:2:1] - **PDS** = distribution of essential commodities to a large number of people through a **network of Fair Price (ration) Shops at subsidised prices**; food procured by FCI goes to the poorer sections.
[39:2:2] - **Main aim:** **food security for the poor** – to **protect the low-income / vulnerable sections against high prices** by guaranteeing a minimum quantity at affordable prices; also checks **hoarding and black-marketing** and stabilises prices ("all of the above").
[39:2:3] - **Procurement at MSP** ensures **stable farm prices, remunerative prices to farmers and food stocks for the PDS** – all three.
[39:2:4] # Evolution
[39:2:5] TABLE head: Stage | Year | Fact
  [39:2:5.0] Rationing | 1940s | World War II / Bengal famine backdrop; revived in the 1960s food shortage
  [39:2:5.1] Buffer stock | Fourth Plan (1969-74) | Formally introduced
  [39:2:5.2] ICDS / Food-for-Work | 1975 / 1977-78 | Food intervention programmes after NSSO poverty data
  [39:2:5.3] RPDS | 1992 | Revamped PDS for remote and backward blocks
  [39:2:5.4] TPDS | June 1997 (not 1985) | BPL/APL differential prices
  [39:2:5.5] Antyodaya Anna Yojana | 25 Dec 2000 | 1 crore poorest BPL families; 25 kg at ₹2 wheat/₹3 rice → 35 kg from April 2002
  [39:2:5.6] Annapurna | 2000 | 10 kg free grain to indigent senior citizens
  [39:2:5.7] NFSA | 2013 | Rights-based
  [39:2:5.8] PMGKAY | 2020 | Extra free grain
[39:2:6] # State food schemes
[39:2:7] TABLE head: State | Scheme
  [39:2:7.0] Andhra Pradesh | NTR's ₹2 a kg rice scheme (1983): up to 25 kg per household per month
  [39:2:7.1] Chhattisgarh | Chhattisgarh Food Security Act, 2012 – the first State Right to Food law, before NFSA
  [39:2:7.2] Uttarakhand | Atal Khadyanna Yojana (2011): APL 10 kg wheat + 10 kg rice at ₹4 and ₹6/kg; BPL at ₹2 and ₹3/kg
  [39:2:7.3] Tamil Nadu | About 94% of fair price shops run by cooperatives
[39:2:8] # Laws and bodies
[39:2:9] TABLE head: Law / body | Year | Purpose
  [39:2:9.0] Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act | 1937 | AGMARK
  [39:2:9.1] Prevention of Food Adulteration Act | 1954 | Replaced by FSSA 2006
  [39:2:9.2] Essential Commodities Act | 1955 | Controls production, supply, price and stocks; base for PDS control orders
  [39:2:9.3] Food Corporations Act | 1964 | Creates FCI
  [39:2:9.4] NCCF | 1965 | Price stabilisation; Consumer Affairs Ministry
  [39:2:9.5] Food Safety and Standards Act | 2006 | Replaced PFA Act 1954; created FSSAI (under the Ministry of Health; its head is a Chairperson, not the DG Health Services)
  [39:2:9.6] Article 47 (DPSP) | – | Raise nutrition and standard of living
[39:2:10] - **Procurement prices** = prices at which government buys grain for PDS and buffer stock.
[39:2:11] > Match angle: ECA 1955 – Grading and Marking 1937 – PFA 1954 – FSSA 2006.
[39:2:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC 03 p.8-9 (PDS, ration shops, rationing 1940s, ICDS 1975, FFW 1977-78); NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC 20 p.9 (PDS objectives); OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.27-28 (RPDS 1992, TPDS 1997, AAY Dec 2000, 25 → 35 kg); Rocket Indian Economy p.8 (MSP → stocks → PDS); app notes 3:39 sub 2, 7
## SUB 3 | Food-based Safety Nets – Mid-Day Meal and ICDS
[39:3:0] TABLE head: Programme | Support | Year
  [39:3:0.0] PDS / NFSA | Grain through Fair Price Shops | –
  [39:3:0.1] ICDS | Supplementary nutrition at anganwadis (0-6, pregnant, lactating) | 1975
  [39:3:0.2] Food-for-Work | Grain as wages | 1977-78
  [39:3:0.3] Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN | Hot cooked meal in schools (Bal Vatika to upper primary); Ministry of Education | 1995 (15 Aug 1995)
[39:3:1] - **PDS, ICDS and Mid-Day Meal** all provide a **food-based safety net** ("all of the above").
[39:3:2] - Mid-Day Meal: encourages attendance and retention and improves nutrition. Corporate partners in Rajasthan: **Adamya Chetna Trust, Havells, Hindustan Zinc, DSCL Kota** (Shriram).
[39:3:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC 03 p.3, p.9 (mid-day meal, ICDS 1975, FFW 1977-78); Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 10th ed. part 04 p.165 (ICDS, MDMS, TPDS as food security programmes); app notes 3:39 sub 5
## SUB 4 | PMGKAY, One Nation One Ration Card, Buffer Stocks and Price Interventions
[39:4:0] # PMGKAY
[39:4:1] - **Announced 26 March 2020** (COVID relief, PM Garib Kalyan package): **5 kg free grain per person** per month on top of NFSA.
[39:4:2] - **Sept 2022:** extended by **three months** (Oct-Dec 2022) beyond 30 Sep 2022.
[39:4:3] - From **1 Jan 2023** merged with NFSA – the **entire NFSA allocation became free** (AAY 35 kg per family; PHH 5 kg per person).
[39:4:4] - Extended for five years **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**; covers about **81.35 crore** people; ~₹11.80 lakh crore by the Centre.
[39:4:5] # One Nation One Ration Card
[39:4:6] - Runs on **IM-PDS** (Integrated Management of PDS, 2018) – nationwide portability and de-duplication.
[39:4:7] - Started **Aug 2019** in 4 States (AP-Telangana, Gujarat-Maharashtra); **Assam** became the **36th and last** State/UT (**June 2022**); now in all 36 States/UTs covering nearly 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries.
[39:4:8] - **Mera Ration** app (DFPD with NIC) for migrants.
[39:4:9] # Buffer stocks
[39:4:10] - **CACP** advises MSP → **FCI** procures wheat and rice → **CCEA** fixes minimum norms **each quarter** (1 Apr, 1 Jul, 1 Oct, 1 Jan) → sold at issue price in deficit areas, or via OMSS.
[39:4:11] TABLE head: Quarter | Norm (rice + wheat)
  [39:4:11.0] 1 April | 210.4 lakh tonnes
  [39:4:11.1] 1 July | 411.2 lakh tonnes (highest)
  [39:4:11.2] 1 October | 307.7 lakh tonnes
  [39:4:11.3] 1 January | 214.1 lakh tonnes
[39:4:12] - **Strategic reserve:** **5 million tonnes** above operational stocks (**30 LT wheat + 20 LT rice**).
[39:4:13] - **OMSS:** **FCI** sells surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices – raises supply, cools prices, clears stock; does not replace procurement.
[39:4:14] - **Anna Darpan** (FCI, 2024; Coforge as system integrator): microservices-based supply chain system **replacing the Depot Online System**, covering mandis, mills, depots and all office levels; an **FCI / Department of Food and Public Distribution** project, not the Agriculture Ministry.
[39:4:15] # Bharat brand
[39:4:16] - **Bharat Rice** (**Feb 2024**) at **₹29/kg**; Bharat Atta and dal – via **NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar** outlets and mobile vans to curb inflation.
[39:4:17] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 10th ed. part 04 p.160-161 (buffer stock, issue price, OMSS); Economic Survey 2025-26 Summary 01 p.54 (ONORC in all 36 States/UTs, ~80 crore); Economic Survey 2025-26 Highlights 01 p.23 (PMGKAY continued); gktoday.in and maritimegateway.com on Anna Darpan (web search result summaries; pages not opened); app notes 3:39 sub 8, 9
## SUB 5 | National Food Security Mission and Global Initiatives
[39:5:0] - **NFSM (2007-08):** Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the **Ministry of Agriculture**, launched in pursuance of the **National Development Council resolution (29 May 2007)** – the APPSC 2011 key calls it the "**National Food Security Resolution**"; targets for the end of the **Eleventh Plan**.
[39:5:1] - **Crops:** originally **rice, wheat and pulses**; **coarse cereals** added only from 2014-15 (12th Plan) – so "not covered" (2010) = coarse cereals.
[39:5:2] - **Global Food Security Platform** (2022, $6 billion): launched by the **International Finance Corporation (IFC)** of the World Bank Group to help the private sector respond to the food crisis.
[39:5:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 3:39 sub 2 (NFSM, NDC resolution); general knowledge for the IFC platform and NFSM crop list, not checked
## SUB 6 | Andhra Pradesh PDS and Hunger Indices
[39:6:0] # AP PDS
[39:6:1] - **Doorstep delivery (Door Delivery System):** from Sept 2019 (Srikakulam pilot) sortex rice delivered to homes, later by **Mobile Dispensing Units** (2021) with electronic weighing – to stop under-weighment, poor quality and leakages; MDUs ended **1 June 2025**, fair price shops restored; doorstep kept for **65+ and the disabled**.
[39:6:2] - **2024-25:** **29,796** Fair Price Shops; 1.48 crore cards; AAY 35 kg/card free; PHH 5 kg/unit free; **ragi** (all) and **jowar** (Rayalaseema) up to **3 kg per card** free in place of rice; wheat 1 kg at ₹16.
[39:6:3] - **Rice card (Feb 2020):** replaced white ration cards; only for PDS rice, **delinked from Aarogyasri** and fee reimbursement.
[39:6:4] - **Mee Mart** (Jul 2026): AP Civil Supplies + **NCCF**; first at **Lalupuram near Guntur**; to link with the **Digital Rupee (CBDC)**.
[39:6:5] # Hunger indices
[39:6:6] - **GHI 2025:** India **102nd of 123**, score **25.8** – "**serious**" (2024: 105th).
[39:6:7] - **GHI publisher:** **Welthungerhilfe** with partners; four indicators: **undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality** (not adult literacy).
[39:6:8] - India's objections: **three of four indicators** concern children only; undernourishment from a **small opinion-poll-type sample**.
[39:6:9] - **SOFI** (*State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World*): led by **FAO** with IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, WHO. **SOFI 2026:** about 645 million hungry in 2025; **Africa (~309 million)** overtook Asia.
[39:6:10] ~~ Sources: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.44-45 (29,796 FPS, 1.48 crore beneficiaries, MDUs); app notes 3:39 sub 10

=== NOTES 3:40 | Rural Development – Issues, Programmes, Rural Infrastructure (pmgsy, Pmay-g, Jal Jeevan Mission)
## SUB 0 | Community Development and Early Rural Programmes (1948-1980)
[40:0:0] # Early community development
[40:0:1] - **Etawah Pilot Project:** **September 1948**, Meheva village near Etawah (UP); by **Lt. Col. Albert Mayer** (American town planner); UP Govt + Point-4 programme; the **first rural-development pilot project**.
[40:0:2] - **Community Development Programme:** **2 October 1952**; the **first rural development programme**; aim – overall development and **improving the standard of living** of rural people through people's participation; it **set the stage for Panchayati Raj**.
[40:0:3] - **National Extension Service:** **1953**; the **first programme of community development** (NextGen); CDP could not cover all India as funds were short.
[40:0:4] - **S.K. Dey:** **architect of community development** in India; first Cooperation and Panchayati Raj Minister.
[40:0:5] - **Balwantrai Mehta Committee:** reviewed CDP and NES; report **November 1957**; **democratic decentralisation** → Panchayati Raj (Rajasthan, then **Andhra Pradesh, 1959**).
[40:0:6] - **Gandhiji's approach:** **Samagra Gramseva** (constructive programme for the whole village).
[40:0:7] # Chronology
[40:0:8] TABLE head: Programme | Year
  [40:0:8.0] Employment Guarantee Scheme (Maharashtra) | 1972
  [40:0:8.1] ARWSP (rural water) | 1972-73
  [40:0:8.2] DPAP (Fourth Plan) | 1973-74
  [40:0:8.3] Minimum Needs Programme | 1974 (Fifth Plan)
  [40:0:8.4] Food for Work | 1977-78
  [40:0:8.5] Desert Development Programme (hot and cold deserts) | 1977-78
  [40:0:8.6] Antyodaya (Rajasthan) | 1977-78
  [40:0:8.7] IRDP experimental / nationwide | 1978-79 / 2 Oct 1980
  [40:0:8.8] TRYSEM | 15 Aug 1979
  [40:0:8.9] NREP | 1980
  [40:0:8.10] Indira Awaas Yojana | 1985-86 (under RLEGP → JRY sub-scheme 1989 → independent 1 Jan 1996)
[40:0:9] - **Order:** CDP (1952) → DPAP (1973-74) → Food for Work (1977-78) → TRYSEM (1979). With IRDP: most keys put **IRDP (1980) after TRYSEM (1979)**, though IRDP began experimentally in 1978-79.
[40:0:10] - **Garibi Hatao** – first in the **Fifth Plan**.
[40:0:11] # Minimum Needs Programme (1974)
[40:0:12] - Network of basic services for **rural and urban** people: elementary and adult education, rural health, **rural water supply**, rural roads, rural electrification, rural housing, **environmental improvement of urban slums**, nutrition. **Social forestry is NOT a component.**
[40:0:13] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Economy p.4-5 (Etawah 1948, NES 1953 first programme of CD, FFW 1977-78, IRDP 1978-79/1980, Antyodaya, Garibi Hatao, CDP 1952); NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC 20 p.1 (CDP in the First Plan); app notes 3:40 sub 0
## SUB 1 | Bharat Nirman (2005-2009)
[40:1:0] - **Launched December 2005** (2005-06) – a **rural infrastructure** programme; targets to be met by the end of **2009**.
[40:1:1] - **Six components:** **irrigation, drinking water, electrification (RGGVY), roads (PMGSY), housing (IAY) and rural telephony**.
[40:1:2] - **Irrigation component:** Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme, **inter-linking of river projects**, **repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies**; rehabilitation of people displaced by irrigation projects was NOT included.
[40:1:3] - **Drinking water:** **National Rural Drinking Water Programme** – renamed from **ARWSP (1972-73)** on **1 April 2009**; now **Jal Jeevan Mission** (2019).
[40:1:4] - **NOT in Bharat Nirman:** **education / Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan**, **NRLM**, agro-based industries, **rural hospitals**.
[40:1:5] - **Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana:** **April 2005** – electrify all villages; subsumed in DDUGJY (2015). **Saubhagya** (2017, PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) – **Ministry of Power**, every household electrified.
[40:1:6] - **National Food for Work Programme:** **14 November 2004** in the **150 most backward districts**; merged into NREGA (2006).
[40:1:7] > NOT angle: SSA, NRLM, rural hospitals, agro-industries, education are outside the six.
[40:1:8] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 10th ed. part 05 p.13, p.32 (Bharat Nirman rural infrastructure; roads one of its six components); app notes 3:40 sub 0, 1
## SUB 2 | PMGSY – Rural Roads
[40:2:0] - **Launched 25 December 2000** (Ministry of Rural Development) – the earliest of PMGSY, DDU-GKY (2014), SAGY (2014) and DAY (2014-16).
[40:2:1] - **Objective:** a **single all-weather road** connecting eligible unconnected habitations to the main road network – **develop the road network to villages** / community life in villages not well connected.
[40:2:2] - **Target year:** connect habitations of **1,000+ by 2003** and **500+ by 2007** (end of the Tenth Plan) – the "full connectivity" target year asked = **2007**.
[40:2:3] TABLE head: Area | Population norm
  [40:2:3.0] Plains | 500+
  [40:2:3.1] Hill States, NE, deserts, Schedule V/tribal areas | 250+
  [40:2:3.2] LWE-affected blocks | 100+ (not 250+)
  [40:2:3.3] Phase | Focus
  [40:2:3.4] PMGSY-I (2000) | New roads
  [40:2:3.5] PMGSY-II (2013) | Upgradation
  [40:2:3.6] PMGSY-III (2019) | Through routes and major rural links
[40:2:4] - **2016-17:** about **130 km of road built per day** (47,350 km in the year – a record).
[40:2:5] - **Meri Sadak** app (2015): citizens' complaints on PMGSY road quality.
[40:2:6] - **2014 initiative:** inclusion of **women SHGs in the transect walk** for road planning.
[40:2:7] - 99.6% of targeted eligible habitations connected (Aug 2026).
[40:2:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP Economy STATIC-1 02 p.1 (PMGSY to connect roadless villages); app notes 3:40 sub 2, 3; general knowledge for the 2007 target, Meri Sadak and transect walk, not checked
## SUB 3 | Rurbanisation – PURA and SPMRM
[40:3:0] # PURA
[40:3:1] - **PURA** = **Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas** – **Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** (explained on the eve of the **54th Republic Day, 2003**); elaborated in ***Target 3 Billion*** (co-author **Srijan Pal Singh**).
[40:3:2] - Aim: **economic upliftment of villages and poverty eradication**; **bridging the rural-urban divide**. Joint AP pilot: Miryalaguda (2004).
[40:3:3] # Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM)
[40:3:4] - **Rurban** (not "Rural/Revival") Mission; launched **21 Feb 2016** (not 2015) at **Kurubhat, Rajnandgaon (Chhattisgarh)**; successor of PURA.
[40:3:5] - Aim: **300 Rurban clusters** – "a rural soul with urban amenities"; curb **distress migration**; make rural areas **socially, economically and physically sustainable** regions.
[40:3:6] - Objectives: **stimulate local economic development**, enhance basic services, create well-planned clusters (not literacy, sex ratio or free power).
[40:3:7] - Funding: **convergence** (MGNREGA, PMGSY, SBM, PMAY) + **Critical Gap Funding up to 30%**; Centre:State **60:40**, **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
[40:3:8] - Cluster: contiguous villages of **25,000-50,000** population (plain/coastal). **Rurban cluster** = rural areas with rising density, non-farm jobs, growing economic activity.
[40:3:9] - AP: **6 clusters** in the second phase (APPSC key); MoRD classified **359 AP panchayats** under Rurban clusters (Mar 2026).
[40:3:10] - SPMRM does NOT replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.
[40:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP Economy STATIC-1 01 p.15 (PURA, Miryalaguda); OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.13 (SPMRM – MoRD, integrated infrastructure); app notes 3:40 sub 6
## SUB 4 | Rural Institutions, Missions and Other Schemes
[40:4:0] TABLE head: Institution / scheme | Fact
  [40:4:0.0] CAPART (1 Sep 1986) | Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology – autonomous body under the Ministry of Rural Development, New Delhi; funds voluntary organisations, promotes rural technology, helps and evaluates rural welfare schemes
  [40:4:0.1] NIRDPR | National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj – Hyderabad
  [40:4:0.2] Mission Antyodaya (Budget 2017-18) | Rural development convergence framework to make GPs poverty-free; annual GP ranking survey
  [40:4:0.3] DRDA | District organ implementing MoRD anti-poverty programmes
  [40:4:0.4] ITDA / TADP | Raise farm output (modern inputs, horticulture, fruit plantations); tribal livelihoods
  [40:4:0.5] Gram Uday se Bharat Uday Abhiyan | 14-24 April 2016; launched at Mhow on Dr B.R. Ambedkar's birth anniversary; strengthens Panchayati Raj
  [40:4:0.6] PM Rural Development Fellows (2011) | Knowledge partner TISS
  [40:4:0.7] PYKKA | Panchayat Yuva Krida aur Khel Abhiyan – community coaches called Kridashrees
  [40:4:0.8] Backward Regions Grant Fund | Launched 2007 (2006-07); about 250 backward districts, not all districts; regional imbalance
  [40:4:0.9] Rural Housing Interest Subsidy Scheme (2017) | 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 lakh for rural houses outside PMAY-G
  [40:4:0.10] Vibrant Villages Programme | Budget 2022-23; Home Affairs; northern border villages; VVP-II approved April 2025 for other land borders
  [40:4:0.11] DPAP / DDP / NWDPRA | DPAP and DDP – Rural Development (Land Resources); NWDPRA – Agriculture – so the UPSC 2014 pairs are all wrong
[40:4:1] - **Budget:** about **₹1 lakh crore** for rural development in 2017-18 (₹1,05,448 crore for the Department of Rural Development).
[40:4:2] - Gram Panchayats without own building in 2016: about **58,000** (APPSC key).
[40:4:3] - Livelihood base: **MGNREGA** wage work; **NRLM** – SHG-based self-employment.
[40:4:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 3:40 sub 1, 2; tiss.txt (library, PMRDF); general knowledge for CAPART, NIRD, BRGF and RHISS, not checked
## SUB 5 | Rural Water and Sanitation – JJM and SBM-G
[40:5:0] # Sanitation
[40:5:1] TABLE head: Scheme | Fact
  [40:5:1.0] Nirmal Gram Puraskar (Oct 2003) | Award for open-defecation-free GPs, blocks, districts, States – boosted the Total Sanitation Campaign
  [40:5:1.1] Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (2012) | Renewed Total Sanitation Campaign – ODF rural India, WASH approach (not slum toilets or housing)
  [40:5:1.2] SBM-G Phase II | Approved Feb 2020 for 2020-21 to 2024-25; ODF Plus – sustain ODF + solid and liquid waste management; ₹1,40,881 crore
  [40:5:1.3] 10-Year Rural Sanitation Strategy | 2019-2029; DDWS, Jal Shakti, 27 Sep 2019
[40:5:2] - **ODF sustainability convergence:** MGNREGS, NRDWP, **RuRBAN** and Atal Bhujal (not PMGSY or AMRUT).
[40:5:3] - **PMAY-G convergence:** SBM-G, NRDWP, DDUGJY, **Ujjwala** and MGNREGS – all.
[40:5:4] - Drinking Water and Sanitation: separate Ministry in **2011** → Department under **Ministry of Jal Shakti** since **June 2019**.
[40:5:5] # Jal Jeevan Mission
[40:5:6] - **Announced in Budget 2019-20**, launched **15 Aug 2019** (Jal Shakti): **Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC)** to every rural household + schools, anganwadis, GP buildings, health centres – originally **by 2024**.
[40:5:7] - **Census 2011:** only about **31%** of rural households had tap water (30.8%).
[40:5:8] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [40:5:8.0] Service level | 55 litres per capita per day of prescribed quality
  [40:5:8.1] Har Ghar Jal village | Tap for every household and institution, certified by Gram Sabha resolution
  [40:5:8.2] Jal Arpan | Handover of schemes to GPs
  [40:5:8.3] Sujal Gaon ID | Digital ID for every rural piped scheme
[40:5:9] - Target **19.36 crore** households; **15.86 crore (81.94%)** connected (Aug 2026); about 18% still unconnected.
[40:5:10] - Deadline **2024** → **December 2028** as **JJM 2.0** (Cabinet, Mar 2026): from infrastructure creation to **service delivery** including O&M; outlay ₹8.69 lakh crore.
[40:5:11] TABLE head: States | Sharing
  [40:5:11.0] Himalayan/NE States + UTs with legislature | 90:10
  [40:5:11.1] Other States | 50:50
  [40:5:11.2] UTs without legislature | 100% Centre
[40:5:12] ~~ Sources: app notes 3:40 sub 1, 2, 5, 7; general knowledge for Census 2011 tap-water share and convergence lists, not checked
## SUB 6 | Housing – PMAY-G and PMAY-U
[40:6:0] - **Indira Awaas Yojana** (1985-86): began under RLEGP, a **sub-scheme of Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** from 1989, independent from **1 Jan 1996**; restructured as **PMAY-G (2016)**.
[40:6:1] - **PMAY-G:** unit assistance **₹1.20 lakh (plains)** / **₹1.30 lakh (hilly/difficult)**; beneficiaries from **SECC 2011** housing-deprivation data, verified by the **Gram Sabha**.
[40:6:2] - Target **2.95 crore** houses by March 2024; Cabinet (9 Aug 2024) approved **2 crore more** for **2024-25 to 2028-29**; 3.13 crore completed by mid-2026.
[40:6:3] - **PMAY-U:** in June 2019 the Housing Ministry **advanced** the 1-crore-house deadline **from 2022 to 2020**; later extended to Dec 2024 and PMAY-U 2.0.
[40:6:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP Economy STATIC-1 02 p.1 (Indira Awas Yojana 1985); businesstoday.in (PMAY-U deadline advanced to 2020; web search summary, page not opened); app notes 3:40 sub 4
## SUB 7 | Rural Infrastructure Gaps and Andhra Pradesh
[40:7:0] TABLE head: Remaining gaps | Achievements
  [40:7:0.0] Piped water: ~18% households unconnected | Saubhagya: 100% willing-household electrification
  [40:7:0.1] O&M of water schemes, housing, last-mile roads | SBM-G: 12.19 crore toilets; 1,288 GOBARdhan plants
  [40:7:0.2] Poor quality, irregularities, cost overruns in JJM works | 5.68 lakh ODF Plus villages
[40:7:1] - Rural infrastructure gaps = piped water, O&M, housing, last-mile roads (**not high-speed rail**).
[40:7:2] - **16th Finance Commission:** one-time "Urbanisation Premium" for merging peri-urban villages.
[40:7:3] # Andhra Pradesh
[40:7:4] - **NTR Sujala** (2014): **safe purified drinking water** to every village household (₹2 per 20 litres).
[40:7:5] - AP households with piped drinking water **2007-08: 63.9%** (APPSC key).
[40:7:6] - **JJM in AP:** FHTC **73%** (70.04 lakh households, 31 Mar 2024); 112 water testing labs; JJM 2.0 goal – every household by 2028. **Madanapalle Water Grid** – drought-prone Rayalaseema.

[40:7:9] - **AP Panchayat Raj sanitation norms** (distance of cattle sheds and toilets from houses and water sources): no checked source – left unkeyed.

=== NOTES 3:41 | Rural Credit and Rural Non-farm Sector; Migration and Rural Distress
## SUB 0 | Rural Credit – History, Surveys and Sources
[41:0:0] # History and surveys
[41:0:1] - **1951:** **moneylenders ~70%** of rural credit; institutional (government, cooperatives, banks) only about **5-7%** – the "modern lending institutions" share asked in APPSC = **about 5%**.
[41:0:2] - **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee** (RBI, 1951; report 1954), chair **A.D. Gorwala**: "**Rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**" → **SBI (1 July 1955)** from the **Imperial Bank of India**.
[41:0:3] - **1969:** social banking and multi-agency approach; **NABARD (1982)** coordinates rural finance – the **apex rural development bank**.
[41:0:4] - **AIDIS 2019** (NSS **77th round**): rural debt **66% institutional**, 34% non-institutional.
[41:0:5] - **NAFIS 2021-22** (NABARD): rural household income **₹12,698**/month; indebted households 47.4% → **52.0%**.
[41:0:6] # Sources
[41:0:7] TABLE head: Institutional | Non-institutional
  [41:0:7.0] Commercial banks, RRBs, cooperatives/PACS, Small Finance Banks, SHG-bank linkage | Moneylenders, traders, landlords, relatives
[41:0:8] - **Kisan Credit Card:** valid **5 years**; open to **tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs, JLGs** (not only landowners).
[41:0:9] - **Small Finance Banks:** lend to small businesses, small and marginal farmers, rural entrepreneurs (not to financial-sector regulators).
[41:0:10] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.20 (moneylenders and debt trap, 1969 social banking, NABARD 1982); Rocket Indian Economy p.3 (SBI 1 July 1955 from Imperial Bank, NABARD 1982); app notes 3:41 sub 0, 1
## SUB 1 | Informal Debt, Debt Trap and Microfinance
[41:1:0] TABLE head: Debt type | Meaning
  [41:1:0.0] Temporary | Seasonal, repaid after harvest
  [41:1:0.1] Chronic | Long-standing
  [41:1:0.2] Debt trap | Taking a new loan (debt) to repay an old one – for a household or a country
[41:1:1] - Usurious interest → distress sale of land/gold, bonded-labour-like ties; often the trigger in farmer suicides.
[41:1:2] - **Microfinance route (DAY-NRLM):** **SHGs, JLGs, BC Sakhis** (not moneylenders); Kerala's **Kudumbashree** (1995 thrift and credit society).
[41:1:3] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Economy 05 p.20 (debt trap, SHGs, Kudumbashree); app notes 3:41 sub 2
## SUB 2 | MGNREGA, Migration and Rural Distress
[41:2:0] # MGNREGA and distress
[41:2:1] - **NREGA** passed 2005, in force 2006, renamed **MGNREGA 2009**: **100 days** per household; wages within **15 days** (not 30); **one-third** women. Now replaced by **VB-G RAM G**.
[41:2:2] - **Positive results:** **higher purchasing power of the rural poor** and **less distress migration** to cities; it **raised** (not reduced) labourers' bargaining power.
[41:2:3] - Person-days **389.09 crore (2020-21) → 183.77 crore** (2025-26, to Dec 2025); urban wages **1.7-2 times** rural (ES 2025-26).
[41:2:4] - AP: **125 days** wage work in distressed pockets under VB-G RAM G (Jun 2026).
[41:2:5] # Migration
[41:2:6] TABLE head: Push (rural) | Pull (urban)
  [41:2:6.0] Few jobs, low wages, landlessness, crop failure, debt | High labour demand, better wages
  [41:2:6.1] Poor health and schools | Education, healthcare
  [41:2:6.2] Unbalanced rural-urban development | Industry and services
[41:2:7] - Causes of rural-urban migration: urban labour demand, unbalanced development, few rural jobs – **all of the above**.
[41:2:8] - **Distress migration:** forced by debt, landlessness, crop loss. **Seasonal:** for a season, then return. **26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants (2020-21).
[41:2:9] - **AP:** distress belts **Rayalaseema, Srikakulam**; Gulf migration from **YSR Kadapa, Godavari/Konaseema**; **93.2%** agricultural households indebted (highest, NSSO 77th round); ~**50%** of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit (NABARD; not 25%).
[41:2:10] # Rural connectivity gap
[41:2:11] - **TRAI:** urban teledensity is about **three times** rural teledensity (APPSC key; e.g. urban ~155 vs rural ~57 in 2018).
[41:2:12] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 10th ed. part 04 p.165 (MGNREGA 100 days for food security); app notes 3:41 sub 4, 5, 7
## SUB 3 | Rural Non-farm Sector and Feminisation of Agriculture
[41:3:0] # Non-farm sector
[41:3:1] - Components: rural industries, Khadi & Village Industries, handloom/handicrafts, food processing, trade, transport, services (**not crop cultivation**).
[41:3:2] TABLE head: Body / scheme | Role
  [41:3:2.0] KVIC | Statutory, KVI Act 1956; Ministry of MSME; implements PMEGP
  [41:3:2.1] SVEP | Under DAY-NRLM; funds rural non-farm enterprises
  [41:3:2.2] MSMEs | 8.7 crore units, ~31.1% of GDP
  [41:3:2.3] DDU-GKY | Placement-linked skilling; parliamentary panel flags low wages and drop-outs
[41:3:3] # Feminisation of agriculture
[41:3:4] - Rising share of women among cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers as **men move to non-farm/urban work** (male out-migration); participation, not land ownership.
[41:3:5] - **Claudia Goldin** (2023 Nobel): **U-shaped curve** – high in the 1980s, fell 2004-05 to 2012, rising after 2020.
[41:3:6] - Rural women = **80%** of the rise in female workers (2017-18 to 2023-24).
